{{Quote|I saved you then. I will not save you now.|Scourge, to Tenebrae in Satele's Mindscape|<ref name="Echoes of Oblivion">{{TORcite|type=general|Echoes of Oblivion|Odessen}}</ref>}}
[[File:Scourge_in_Echoes_of_Oblivion.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Scourge faces Tenebrae inside Satele Shan's mindscape.]]
Later, in the year [[3626 BBY]]<ref name="Date">{{TOR_updates|6.2}}</ref>, Scourge and Kira Carsen, with the aid of [[T7-O1]], were able to locate the [[Kira Carsen's ship|vessel]] that they had placed Satele and her students aboard. With the aid of the Alliance Commander, they made their way onboard in order to stop [[Tenebrae]] from fully resurrecting himself. Aboard the ship, they were attacked by remnants of the [[Hand of the Empire|Emperor's Hand]], led by [[Servant Four]], whom they fought with in order to get to Satele. Kira Carsen then led them in a ritual that allowed them to enter [[Mindscape|Satele Shan's mind]].<ref name="Echoes of Oblivion" />

Once inside, Scourge, Carsen, and the Alliance Commander fought their way to the center of the mindscape, aided along the way by the spirits of [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], [[Meetra Surik]], and [[Darth Marr]]. Once at the center, they fought against the Emperor, alongside the spirits of all those that had been victimized by Tenebrae over the centuries. After a long-fought battle, they were successfully able to vanquish the Sith Emperor once and for all.<ref name="Echoes of Oblivion" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I still remember the feel of sunlight on my skin. The scent of favorite foods. The color of my first love's eyes. To experience those simple pleasures again would be worth anything.''"<br />"''This is why Jedi don't form attachments. Desire unbalances you.''"<br />"''You misunderstand everything. My equilibrium never deviates. I feel&hellip; nothing.|Scourge and the Hero of Tython|<ref name="Eternal Emptiness">{{TORcite|type=conversation|Lord Scourge|Eternal Emptiness}}</ref>}}
[[File:Lord_Scourge_Valiant.png|thumb|left|190px|Lord Scourge]]
A pureblood Sith with [[Color/Legends|crimson]] skin and facial tendrils, Scourge had bright red [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]<ref name="Holonet" /> and a thick-chested torso. Scourge was ambitious and power-hungry in the years before he became immortal,<ref name="Revan" /> and his arrogance and pride were among the few emotions<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> that remained after the Emperor's immortality ritual stripped him of his senses and humanity. The ritual warped Scourge's ability to process his environment in the fashion that others did; he was physically incapable of feeling simple pleasures, such as the scent of his favorite [[Foodstuff/Legends|foods]] or the warmth of sunlight, though not to the point that his physical abilities were compromised. As a result, he grew to treasure the memories of the things that he could no longer sense or feel.<ref name="What Was Lost" /> Scourge was sardonic and grimly fatalistic,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> and he developed a uniquely cynical viewpoint during his centuries of service, as he observed how his fellow Sith seemed unable to change their self-destructive ways.<ref name="Wisdom" /> Following the Emperor's final death, Scourge lost his immortality and regained his emotions. Having regained the very things he had been stripped of for centuries led him to realize how much companionship meant to him.<ref name="Onslaught" />

Unlike many of his fellow Sith, Scourge was willing to devote himself to a cause other than his own personal gain, though his Sith mentality made him more than willing to sacrifice his allies in order to advance his cause, as he did to Revan and Meetra Surik.<ref name="Legends">{{TORcite|type=conversation|Lord Scourge|Legends}}</ref> Scourge was intelligent and cunning,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> and he enjoyed using power<ref name="Codex" /> and also manipulating others to his own ends.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> He disliked greed and selfishness but was also disgusted by mercy and other Jedi sentiments that he viewed as weak.<ref name="Codex" /> However, the Sith Lord acknowledged that the strengths of the Jedi were not necessarily lesser than those of the Sith.<ref name="A Dark Past" /> While Scourge respected strength and power, the Emperor's desire to sacrifice all other life just to gain power horrified Scourge, and he devoted himself to stopping the Emperor through any means necessary.<ref name="Revan" /> His duties as the Emperor's Wrath prevented him from ever taking an apprentice, and because of the effects of the immortality ritual, the Sith was unable and unwilling to enter romantic relationships or begin a family.<ref name="Scourge Twitter">{{Twitter|hallhood|status/261705208202141696|[[Hall Hood]]|quote=Scourge's duties to the Emperor precluded the taking of an apprentice or a family. He is absolutely alone in the galaxy.|nobackup=1}}</ref>

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|You have a special gift. You do not just feed on the raw emotions of your foe; you gorge yourself on them. You feast on their primal fear. It amplifies your hate and anger. It fuels the power of the Force. It transforms you into an instrument of death and destruction.|Darth Nyriss, to Scourge|<ref name="Revan" />}}
An expert swordsman, Scourge was exceptionally powerful in the Force, and the Jedi Master Revan believed that he had incredible potential. As a Sith Lord, he wielded a blood-red lightsaber with a spiked crossguard and [[Tooth/Legends|fang]]-like hilt, and he was proficient in at least three forms of lightsaber combat: the defensive Soresu form, the overwhelmingly offensive [[Form VII/Legends|Juyo form]], and the acrobatic Ataru form.<ref name="Revan" /> In battle, Scourge made use of both powerful, two-handed strikes and strong, sweeping blows with his lightsaber, and he also utilized [[Unarmed combat/Legends|unarmed combat]] in conjunction with his lightsaber. Scourge often enveloped his fist with lightning during combat and delivered punches to his opponents.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> His skill with the blade, regardless of whether he wielded it with his dominant right hand or his left hand, was such that even his instructors at the Sith Academy had been reluctant to battle him while he was still an apprentice. Scourge's primary gift was the ability to draw strength from the emotions of his opponents, gorging himself on their fear and anger to bolster the strength of the dark side within himself. While his ability initially put him at a disadvantage when facing non-living opponents, as he weakened himself by trying to draw on nonexistent emotions, he learned to overcome his weakness and became just as proficient in fighting droids as any other Sith.<ref name="Revan" />

[[File:Scourge_chokes.png|thumb|right|250px|Scourge uses the Force to choke an Imperial soldier]]
Scourge was skilled in using the Force to [[Force sense/Legends|sense]] enemies in his surroundings, and he made frequent use of telekinesis in combat and as a tool of intimidation. He bolstered his physical abilities with the Force in order to increase his speed and agility, and he could guide a thrown lightsaber with the Force to strike his intended target in the heat of battle. Another of his skills was the ability to wrap the dark side around himself, concealing his presence from others and also keeping him warm.<ref name="Revan" />

Early in his time at the Sith Academy, Scourge showed a natural affinity for interrogation and torture. He had an innate skill at discerning the truth and instinctively knew which questions to ask in order to get the answers he wanted. A master in the art of interrogation, Scourge could also bolster his skills with the power of the dark side, enabling him to dominate the minds of the weak-willed and undermine strong-willed individuals.<ref name="Revan" /> His centuries of service to the Emperor gave him a unique perspective on his fellow Sith; Scourge's skill in interrogation eventually developed to the point that he was able to analyze a person's flaws and personality after only a short period of observation.<ref name="Codex" />

==Equipment==
[[File:Scourge_Lightsaber.png|thumb|left|200px|Scourge's lightsaber hilt]]
After becoming the Emperor's Wrath,<ref name="Revan" /> Scourge received extensive biochemical enhancements throughout his body, which further increased his strength<ref name="Emperor's Wrath" /> and worked to sustain the effects of the immortality ritual that Scourge underwent at the Emperor's hands.<ref name="Revan" /> He was classified as a heavily armored, close-combat assassin,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> wearing a suit of heavy, black, spiked armor and utilizing a [[Personal energy shield/Legends|personal energy shield]] generator to protect himself from blasterfire and most attacks.<ref name="TOR" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Dr. Hannibal Lecter &#43; Ogami Itto &#43; The Lord High Papal from Jim Starlin's 'Dreadstar' comics &#61; Lord Scourge, The Emperor's Wrath.|A Tweet from [[Hall Hood]], writer for the ''Star Wars: The Old Republic'' Jedi Knight class|<ref name="Hood Twitter">{{Twitter|hallhood|status/170553745615237122|[[Hall Hood]]|date=2012-02-17|archivedate=20160115021258}}</ref>}}
Scourge first appeared in the [[2011]] novel ''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]'' by [[Drew Karpyshyn]], a tie-in book to the [[BioWare]]&ndash;[[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', which was released later that year. The novel introduced Scourge and much of the Sith Empire and Emperor's backstory, while also continuing the storylines of Revan and Meetra Surik, who were the player characters in the [[2003]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' and its [[2004]] sequel, [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords|''The Sith Lords'']], respectively. The novel also established the backstory for the Jedi Knight class in ''The Old Republic'', in which Scourge is a companion character for the Jedi Knight who is acquired at the beginning of Act III in the class storyline.

Scourge is voiced by [[Joseph Gatt]] in ''The Old Republic'',<ref name="Manual">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' Credits</ref> and as with all companion characters in the game, the player can gain or lose affection with Scourge depending on chosen actions and choices in cutscenes. Scourge gains affection when the player uses power against the weak or expresses anger, revenge, or spite and loses affection whenever the player makes decisions that are greedy or merciful and when the player submits to Jedi or Republic authorities.<ref name="Holonet" /> The character was excluded as a romance option for the Jedi Knight for a variety of reasons, which included budget limitations, practicality, and creative direction.<ref name="Twitt">{{Twitter|hallhood|status/194480029252599808|[[Hall Hood]]|quote=Many reasons why Scourge isn't a romance, from practical/budgetary to creative direction. Maybe someday...|nobackup=1}}</ref> However, with the release of Onslaught, Scourge has now become a romance opportunity for the Jedi Knight, both male and female.<ref name="Wrath Triumphant">{{TORcite|type=general|Wrath Triumphant|Odessen}}</ref>

As a companion character, Scourge is one of five characters who can be utilized by player characters. Unlike companions like Kira Carsen and T7-O1, he is not required to accompany the player character on any class missions. Therefore, this article assumes only that one of the companions accompanies the Knight on the class missions but does not specify which one. Also, as a Republic character, the Jedi Knight is assumed to be a light-side character; therefore, the Hero of Tython&mdash;the in-game title for the character&mdash;is assumed to choose only options that result in the maximum light-side points.<ref name="Light Side">This article assumes that [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] classes in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' choose the options that provide the most [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-side]] alignment points.</ref> Scourge also receives a number of optional customizations that can alter his skin color, [[Hair/Legends|hair]] color, and hairstyle.

Scourge has received mentions in ''The Old Republic''{{'s}} official site and the [[2012]] reference guide ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', and the ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' gave further information on the character's history and motivations in its summary of the Knight's companions. Scourge also appears as a companion character for the Jedi Knight in ''The Old Republic''{{'s}} paid expansion, [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel|''Rise of the Hutt Cartel'']], but as the expansion can be played by any of the four Republic classes, it is uncertain as to who [[canon]]ically performed the events of the expansion. As such, this article excludes information from the expansion.
